🥘 Ingredients

  • 2 medium zucchinis, sliced into half-moons
  • 3 medium carrots, peeled and thinly sliced
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by prepping your vegetables: slice the zucchinis into half-moons and peel and thinly slice the carrots. This uniform slicing helps them cook evenly and quickly. Using a sharp knife here is key to getting nice, clean cuts that will cook at the same rate. Avoid cutting pieces too thick or uneven, as that can lead to some parts being undercooked while others overdone.
  2. Heat two tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once shimmering but not smoking, add the minced garlic and fresh thyme leaves. Stir constantly for about 30 seconds to release the aromas without burning the garlic, which can turn bitter quickly. This step infuses the oil with flavor that will coat the veggies beautifully.
  3. Add the sliced carrots first since they take a bit longer to cook than zucchini. Stir frequently to coat them in the infused oil. Cooking them first ensures they soften slightly while still holding a bit of crunch. Don’t rush this step by turning the heat too high; a gentle sizzle is perfect to cook them evenly without burning.
  4. Next, add the zucchini slices to the skillet. Stir well so they mix with the carrots and absorb the garlicky oil. Zucchini cooks quickly and releases moisture, so keep the heat at medium to avoid sogginess. Stir often but gently to keep the veggies intact and prevent them from turning mushy.
  5. Season the veggies with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Seasoning at this stage helps bring out the natural sweetness of the carrots and zucchini. Be mindful not to over-salt, especially if you plan to serve this with a salty main dish.
  6. Turn off the heat and drizzle the stir fry with fresh lemon juice. This brightens the dish and adds a subtle tang that balances the sweetness and earthiness of the vegetables. Stir gently to combine. The acid also helps keep the veggies fresh and vibrant.
  7. Transfer the stir fry to a serving dish and sprinkle chopped fresh parsley over the top. Parsley adds a pop of color and a fresh, slightly peppery flavor that complements the other herbs and garlic beautifully. It also makes the dish look more inviting and vibrant.
  8. Serve immediately while warm as a side dish or light main. This stir fry pairs wonderfully with grilled chicken, fish, or tofu. If you want to add protein directly, toss in cooked chickpeas or edamame at the end for a quick boost.
  9. If you have leftovers, cool them completely before storing in an airtight container in the fridge. Reheat gently to preserve the texture. Avoid overheating which can make the veggies limp and watery.

  1. Start by slicing your zucchini into even 1/4-inch thick rounds. This thickness is key because it ensures the zucchini cooks evenly in the air fryer without becoming mushy or drying out.   2. In a shallow bowl, whisk the beaten egg until smooth. In another bowl, combine the panko breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. The panko gives a light crunch, while the Parmesan adds flavor and helps the crust brown beautifully. Mix these dry ingredients well to distribute the spices evenly. When you dip the zucchini into the egg, it creates a sticky surface for the breadcrumb mixture to cling to, ensuring a uniform crust.
  3. Dip each zucchini slice into the beaten egg, making sure it’s fully coated, then press it into the breadcrumb mixture. Don’t just sprinkle the crumbs on; pressing firmly helps the coating stick during air frying. Place each coated slice on a wire rack or plate and repeat until all zucchini slices are coated. If you want extra crispiness, you can double dip—dip again in egg and breadcrumbs for a thicker crust, but keep in mind it will add more cooking time.
  4. Preheat your air fryer to 400°F (200°C) for about 3 minutes. Preheating is important because it jump-starts the crisping process, giving you that golden crust right away. If you skip this, the zucchini might release moisture before the crust sets, resulting in soggy bites. Once preheated, lightly spray the air fryer basket with cooking spray to prevent sticking.
  5. Arrange the coated zucchini slices in a single layer in the air fryer basket, making sure they don’t overlap. Crowding the basket traps steam and prevents crisping. You might need to cook in batches depending on your air fryer size. Lightly spray the tops of the zucchini with cooking spray or olive oil spray; this helps the crust brown evenly and adds a little extra crunch without extra calories.
  6. Air fry the zucchini at 400°F for 10-12 minutes, flipping halfway through. Flipping is crucial because it ensures both sides get that beautiful golden crust. Keep an eye on them during the last few minutes to avoid burning; cooking times can vary by air fryer model. The zucchini should be tender inside but not mushy, with a crispy, cheesy crust outside.
  7. If you want an extra cheesy finish, sprinkle a little extra shredded mozzarella over the zucchini slices as soon as they come out of the air fryer. The residual heat will melt the cheese perfectly without needing extra cooking. This step adds a gooey, melty contrast to the crunchy crust and is my personal favorite touch.
  8. Serve immediately while hot and crispy. These zucchini bites are best enjoyed fresh out of the air fryer for maximum crunch. Pair them with your favorite dipping sauce like marinara, ranch, or a spicy aioli for extra flavor. If you wait too long, the crust can soften as it cools, so timing is key for the best texture experience.
  9. Clean your air fryer basket promptly after cooking to prevent cheese and crumbs from hardening. A quick wipe with a damp cloth while still warm makes cleanup easier and keeps your air fryer in good shape for next time. Regular cleaning also ensures no lingering flavors affect future recipes.

  1. Start by peeling and seeding your cucumbers carefully. This step is crucial because the skin can add bitterness and the seeds contain excess water that can make your salsa watery. If you skip peeling or seeding, your salsa might turn out too watery and lose that fresh crunch we want.
  2. Combine the diced cucumbers, chopped red bell pepper, green chili peppers, onion, cilantro, and minced garlic in a large mixing bowl. Mixing fresh ingredients evenly helps the flavors distribute well. Use fresh herbs and peppers for the best taste, as dried ones won’t provide the same brightness. Take your time chopping finely to ensure every bite is flavorful.
  3. In a small bowl, whisk together white vinegar, lime juice, salt, sugar, and ground cumin until sugar dissolves. This dressing is what gives the salsa its tangy kick and helps preserve it during canning. The vinegar and lime juice provide acidity that balances the sweetness of the sugar and the earthiness of cumin. Make sure the sugar is fully dissolved for an even flavor.
  4. Pour the vinegar mixture over the vegetable mix and toss gently to combine. Coat every piece evenly but avoid smashing the cucumbers, which can release water. This step ensures that the salsa is flavorful throughout and not just on the surface. Be gentle to keep the texture crisp and fresh.
  5. Let the salsa rest in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight. This resting period allows the flavors to meld and the acidity to mellow slightly. It also helps the cucumbers absorb some flavor without losing their crunch. If you skip resting, the salsa might taste less balanced and the cucumbers won’t be as flavorful.
  6. Prepare your canning jars by sterilizing them in boiling water for 10 minutes. Proper sterilization is critical to prevent spoilage and ensure your salsa keeps well. After sterilizing, keep the jars hot until filling. Skipping this step can lead to bacteria growth and unsafe canned goods.
  7. Fill the hot jars with the chilled salsa, leaving about 1/2 inch headspace. Headspace is important to allow for expansion during processing and to create a vacuum seal. Avoid packing the salsa too tightly, which can cause jars to crack or prevent proper sealing.
  8. Wipe rims of jars clean with a damp cloth and place sterilized lids and rings on top, tightening them finger-tight. Clean rims ensure a proper seal, and finger-tight lids allow air to escape during processing. Over-tightening can prevent air release and cause sealing failure.
  9. Process jars in a boiling water bath for 15 minutes, adjusting for altitude if needed. This heat treatment kills any bacteria and seals the jars. Make sure water covers jars by at least 1 inch and start timing once water returns to a boil. Removing jars too early or not boiling long enough risks spoilage.
